_comment: CoreWeave (CRWV) stress-test model, template levered_growth_v1, calibrated 2026-10-18 (scratchpad calibration.md). Base = FY2026 guidance, consensus-like FY2027, the report base for FY2028. Conventions: opening balance sheet pro forma for the Sep-2026 2.875% convertible; amortising loans repay straight-line to maturity (the 10-Q table is more front-loaded); tranche rates = stated rate + fee and discount amortisation (~US$200m a year, so interest matches the income statement and the Q3 guide); opening.dep_base calibrated to the FY2026 adj. operating income guide (no in-service lag in the engine). No NOLs, no interest income, no SBC beyond share_dilution_pct, revenue not linked to capex. Scenario presets are uniform shifts: they cannot keep FY2026 at guidance while cutting FY2027-28. Known gap (no check): FY2027E EPS -7.7 vs consensus -4.33 and FY2028E net income -8.5bn vs ~-2.6bn, from full depreciation, interest on new debt and the report base FY2028 EBITDA below consensus.

prior.note: FY2025 revenue, the base for FY2026 growth.

stub.note: H1 FY2026 = Q1 + Q2. opex_ex_da_sbc is derived so that revenue - cost of revenue - opex = company adjusted EBITDA (1,157 + 1,510); da = adj. EBITDA - adj. operating income (1,136 + 1,382). Capex is the company definition (7.7bn + 9.4bn; XBRL cash capex 14,117). Interest is income-statement interest expense (536 + 640). other_income (-21) closes the gap to reported net income of -1,366.

opening.note: 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, pro forma for the 2.875% convertible issued 22 Sep 2026: cash 5,524 + 3,570 net proceeds after capped calls; equity 5,024 less the ~570 capped-call cost; that convert is in the debt list at 4,200. dep_base: the existing assets that depreciate, calibrated to Q2 2026 D&A (1,382, about 5.5bn a year x 6 years = 33bn) plus part of the 11.9bn of construction in progress entering service in H2; it lands FY2026 adj. operating income inside the guide. Gross PP&E 52,622 includes that construction in progress, which does not depreciate yet.

debt.name: DDTL 1.0 (Magnetar/Blackstone, 2023)
debt.note: Term SOFR + 9.6196%; 10-Q effective rate 15% (incl. fees). Amortises from contract cash flows; modelled straight-line to maturity. Rate here includes ~150bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated SOFR + 962bp).

debt.name: DDTL 2.0 (Blackstone/Magnetar, 2024)
debt.note: Margin set per customer rating: SOFR + 6.00-6.50% (investment-grade contracts) or 13.00% (non-IG). 650bp is our blend; 10-Q effective rate 11%. Rate here includes ~85bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated SOFR + 650bp).

debt.name: DDTL 2.1 (incremental tranche under the DDTL 2.0 agreement, Sep 2025)
debt.note: Term SOFR + 4.25% plus 1.50% upfront fee per draw; each draw matures 5 years after drawing. 10-Q effective rate 9%. Rate here includes ~110bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated SOFR + 425bp).

debt.name: DDTL 3.0 (OpenAI contract, Jul 2025)
debt.note: SOFR + 4.00%; US$2.6bn commitment. 10-Q effective rate 9%. Reported cash-trap clause [s61]. Rate here includes ~135bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated SOFR + 400bp).

debt.name: DDTL 4.0 floating tranche (A3 / A(low), Mar 2026)
debt.note: Daily SOFR + 2.25%. 10-Q: US$1.4bn floating + US$1.5bn fixed outstanding (split pro rata to the US$2,837m principal). Facility requires swaps/hedging; floating exposure may be partly swapped (not disclosed). Rate here includes ~100bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated SOFR + 225bp).

debt.name: DDTL 4.0 fixed tranche
debt.note: UST + 2.00% at draw, about 5.9%. Rate here includes ~50bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 5.9%).

debt.name: DDTL 5.0 (Ba2 / BB+, May 2026)
debt.note: Stated SOFR + 4.50%, but at least 95% must be swapped to fixed, so modelled as fixed at 8.3% (4.50% + an assumed ~3.8% swap rate; not disclosed). 10-Q effective rate 9% incl. fees. Rate here includes ~70bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 8.3%).

debt.name: 9.250% senior notes due 2030
debt.note: Rate here includes ~30bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 9.25%).

debt.name: 9.000% senior notes due Feb 2031
debt.note: Rate here includes ~40bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 9%).

debt.name: 9.750% senior notes due Oct 2031
debt.note: US$1.75bn (Apr 2026) + US$1.0bn add-on at 102.0; yielded ~15.8% on 15 Oct 2026 [s31].

debt.name: 9.625% senior notes due 2032
debt.note: Traded below 80c, ~15% yield, 14 Oct 2026 [s28]. Rate here includes ~20bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 9.625%).

debt.name: 8.500% EUR senior notes due 2032 (EUR 2.0bn)
debt.note: Swapped to USD with cross-currency swaps (fair-value hedge); the USD-equivalent swapped coupon is not disclosed, so the EUR coupon is used. Rate here includes ~30bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 8.5%).

debt.name: 1.75% convertible senior notes due Dec 2031
debt.note: Conversion ~US$107.80 (capped call to US$215.60) [s107]. Treated as debt (net-share settlement). Rate here includes ~25bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 1.75%).

debt.name: 1.75% convertible senior notes due Oct 2032
debt.note: Conversion rate 8.3612 per US$1,000 = ~US$119.60 (10-Q); capped call to ~US$230 [s107]. Treated as debt. Rate here includes ~25bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 1.75%).

debt.name: OEM and software-licence financing (recourse)
debt.note: Many arrangements maturing Dec 2026 - Jul 2030; 10-Q effective rate 11% (9% on the short-term part). Rate here includes ~50bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 10.5%).

debt.name: Magnetar loan
debt.note: Refund with a multiplier equal to a 12% annual return.

debt.name: Revolving credit facility (US$2.5bn; US$2.0bn available after LCs)
debt.note: Undrawn at 30 Jun 2026 (US$1.0bn drawn at Dec 2025). SOFR + 1.75% per the 2024 facility. Undrawn capacity at 30 Jun: DDTL 4.0 US$5.7bn, DDTL 5.0 US$2.0bn, DDTL 5.5 US$2.6bn, revolver US$2.0bn [s2,s59]; the model funds any gap at the new-debt rate instead.

debt.name: 2.875% convertible senior notes due Apr 2033 (issued 22 Sep 2026)
debt.note: Issued 22 Sep 2026 (after the balance-sheet date; included pro forma). US$4.2bn incl. option; net cash ~US$3.57bn after ~US$0.57bn capped calls. Conversion ~US$97.85 (cap US$199.70). Rate here includes ~25bp a year of issue-cost and discount amortisation (stated 2.875%).

rates.note: **Base = market forwards**: calendar-year averages of the 3M term-SOFR forward curve as of 15 Oct 2026 (end-2026 4.27%, end-2027 4.64%, end-2028 4.71%, end-2029 4.53%) [s122]; 2030 extrapolated (the curve is not public past 2029). 2026 is H2 only: ~3.63% to 16 Sep, 3.88% after the 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% [s111], ~4.08% for Nov–Dec weighting FedWatch odds of ~40–49% for an October hike [s124,s125]. Cross-check: 2-yr Treasury 4.77% on 15 Oct 2026 [s123]. **Alternative = the Fed’s September 2026 projections** (median year-end 4.1% / 4.1% / 3.9% / 3.6%, longer run ~3.25%) [s119,s120,s121,s126]: 3.85 / 4.10 / 4.00 / 3.75 / 3.45% as annual averages, about 75bp below the market path; the "Fed projections" scenario applies it as a −75bp SOFR shift. The SOFR shift also moves the cost of new and refinanced debt one-for-one.

drivers.label: Revenue growth (FY/FY)
drivers.help: Year-on-year revenue growth (fundamental growth). FY2026 path = guidance midpoint US$12.8bn; FY2027 = consensus ~US$26.2bn; FY2028 ~US$38bn (report base); then slowing as the backlog is delivered. The slider shifts every year by the same number of points; in FY2026 it moves only the unreported second half.

drivers.label: Cost of revenue (% of revenue, excl. D&A)
drivers.help: Power, colocation and data-centre operating costs. Rose from ~26% (2024) to 34% in H1 2026 as leased capacity ramped ahead of revenue; we assume modest scale benefits, then pricing pressure on renewals.

drivers.label: Operating expenses (% of revenue, excl. D&A and SBC)
drivers.help: Technology & infrastructure (ex-depreciation), sales & marketing, G&A and R&D. H1 2026 8.4% (Q1 9.9%, Q2 7.2%); operating leverage as revenue doubles. Together with cost of revenue this sets adjusted EBITDA margin (57.5% H2-26, ~60.5% FY27, 62% FY28; consensus FY27 59-63%).

drivers.label: Stock-based compensation (% of revenue)
drivers.help: Non-cash, but a real cost to shareholders (dilution). 12.3% in FY2025 (IPO grants), 6.8% in H1 2026, 6.4% in Q2.

drivers.label: Capex (company definition, US$m)
drivers.help: FY2026 = guidance midpoint US$37bn (raised twice from >US$30bn); FY2027–28 = BofA US$47.4bn / US$49.8bn; tapering after as growth slows. Company definition (includes accrued and vendor-financed additions). Revenue does not follow capex in this model: a capex cut without a revenue cut flatters the result.

drivers.label: GPU / infrastructure useful life
drivers.help: CoreWeave depreciates servers over six years. Bears argue GPUs are economically obsolete in 3–4 years. A shorter life raises depreciation and losses but changes neither EBITDA nor cash flow.

drivers.label: SOFR shift vs market path
drivers.help: Moves the whole SOFR path (base = market forwards, ~4.5% in 2027–29). −75bp is roughly the Fed’s own September projections; +150bp a renewed hiking cycle (September CPI 3.7%). Hits the ~US$11bn of floating DDTL debt at once and, one-for-one, the cost of all new and refinanced debt, which is most of the stack by 2028.

drivers.label: Credit spread shift
drivers.help: Moves the spread on floating debt and on all new or refinanced debt. CoreWeave 5-yr CDS went from ~547bp at end-June to ~1,040bp on 15 Oct 2026; −100bp is a path toward investment grade.

drivers.label: All-in cost of new and refinanced debt
drivers.help: All-in cost of new and refinanced debt at the base SOFR path. Blend of contract-backed DDTL draws (SOFR + 2.25–5.50%, ~6.7–10%), OEM financing (~9–11%), unsecured notes (9.25–9.75% coupons, but ~15% secondary yields in Oct 2026) and converts (1.75–2.875%). 8% = mostly investment-grade DDTLs; 14% = refinancing near today’s unsecured yields.

drivers.label: Share of funding gap met with new equity
drivers.help: CoreWeave has an at-the-market programme for up to 35m shares (~US$2bn at today’s price, ~5% of the 2026–27 funding gap). Higher = less debt, more dilution.

drivers.label: Discount on new shares vs market price
drivers.help: ATM sales are near market (agent commission ~1-2%); a stressed follow-on would price at a deep discount.

drivers.label: Share-count creep from employee equity
drivers.help: Annual growth in shares from RSUs and options, on top of any equity raised. The report base adds about 13.5m SBC shares by end-2027 (about 1.6% a year on 551.5m).

drivers.label: Minimum cash balance
drivers.help: Cash kept on hand; any shortfall is borrowed or raised. US$5.5bn at 30 Jun 2026, about two quarters of cash opex plus interest. DDTL 4.0 also requires restricted cash covering three months of debt service.

drivers.label: Customer prepayments (% of revenue increase)
drivers.help: Customers prepay part of their contracts (deferred revenue US$9.7bn at 30 Jun 2026). Cash inflow modelled as this share of each year's revenue increase. Implied history: ~37% (FY2025), ~90% (H1 2026, lumpy).

drivers.label: Tax rate on positive pre-tax profit
drivers.help: Applies only when pre-tax profit is positive (no loss carry-forwards modelled, so conservative). The base case is loss-making throughout.

drivers.label: Exit EV / EBITDA (on FY2028)
drivers.help: Multiple applied at end-2027 to FY2028 adjusted EBITDA. 7x is just below Oracle's forward ~7.3x; 5.5x is distressed credit; 9x a re-rating as financing goes investment grade.

drivers.label: Cost of equity
drivers.help: Discounts the end-2027 value back to today. Set above the ~15% unsecured bond yield: the equity ranks below US$35bn+ of debt.

drivers.label: Share price (for multiples and new-share pricing)
drivers.help: Close of 16 Oct 2026. Sets the market multiples shown (P/E, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield) and the price of any new shares.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.note: FY2026 at guidance, consensus-like FY2027, FY2028 adj. EBITDA ~US$23.6bn at 7x; market SOFR path; 5% of the funding gap met with equity.

scenarios.name: Bear (funding-constrained)
scenarios.note: The report’s bear: revenue ~US$20bn (FY2027) and ~US$23bn (FY2028) at 52–54% margins, funding at 12% plus 100bp of spread, ~80m new shares at ~US$37, 5.5x. Gives ~US$5 (report ~US$5), net debt ~US$62bn at end-2027 (report ~US$59bn). The presets shift every year, so H2 2026 is cut too; the −30% capex cut moves spend out of H2 2026 but keeps H2 2026 + FY2027 capex at the report’s ~US$42bn.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.note: The report’s bull: revenue ~US$29bn (FY2027) and ~US$45bn (FY2028) at 64–65% margins, FY2028 adj. EBITDA ~US$29.5bn, spreads 50bp tighter as financing moves toward investment grade, 9x. Gives ~US$261 (report ~US$259).

scenarios.name: Restructuring
scenarios.note: The report puts this at ~US$0. The model cannot simulate a default; this stress shows the arithmetic that leads there: debt above enterprise value (value floors at zero) and heavy dilution at half the share price.

scenarios.name: Rates +150bp
scenarios.note: Owner-requested interest-rate stress: inflation re-accelerates (Sep CPI 3.7%) and the Fed keeps hiking; SOFR +150bp, credit spreads +100bp. Both flow into new and refinanced debt.

scenarios.name: Funding at October yields
scenarios.note: New and refinanced debt costs 14%, near the ~15% the unsecured notes yielded in October 2026, instead of 9.5%. Rates and operations at base.

scenarios.name: Fed projections path
scenarios.note: SOFR follows the Fed’s September 2026 projections instead of market forwards (about 75bp lower on average, 2027–30).

valuation.note: As in the report: EV at end-2027 = exit EV/EBITDA x FY2028 adj. EBITDA (one-year-forward), less net debt and over shares at end-2027, discounted to 17 Oct 2026. Convertibles are debt (net-share settlement, capped calls). Leases are excluded.

checks.label: FY2026E D&A consistent with the adj. operating income guide of US$0.96–1.15bn (≈US$7.4bn adj. EBITDA less D&A)
FY2026E interest: H1 actual US$1.18bn + H2 at about twice the Q3 guide of US$860–940m, Q4 higher
FY2027E revenue vs consensus range US$21.1–31.0bn (mean US$26.3bn)
FY2027E adj. EBITDA vs consensus US$15.6–16.6bn
